question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>...100</mo></mrow></mfenced></math>. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> be a relation on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> defined by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi></math> if and only if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>y</mi></math>. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> be a symmetric relation on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and the number of elements in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>. Then the minimum value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is _______.

solution.text:
Given,

2x=3y

⇒x3=y2

Now, let x3=y2=k

⇒x=3k & y=2k

Now, given set A=1, 2, 3, .......,100

So, for k≤33 we get,

⇒R=3,2,6,4,9,6,12,8,....99,66

⇒nR=33

Now, R1 is symmetric relation on A and R⊂R1 so, we need elements 3,2,6,4,9,6,12,8,....99,66, 2,3,4,6,6,9, 8,12,....66,99 in R1

Hence, the minimum number of elements in R1 is 33+33=66
